title: Lord Cobham to Walsingham, May-June 1588 (BL Harley MS 287, DECODE R8490/R8492/R8495/R8496)

steps.what: Fetched DECODE metadata and full-resolution images of R8490-R8497.
CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4, May-June 1588: calendars SP 77 Cobham letters only, not Harley 287.
Tested the catalogue's key record R8497 (f. 187).
Read 'in all LVZLTL' as ARMADA/ARMATA from context.
Found DECODE sibling records R8481, R8488, R8489, R8493 marked Decrypted, with interlinear decipherments.
Rebuilt about 20 letters of the alphabet from the f. 75 and f. 89 glosses; cross-checked with the cypher-7e session's key.
Applied the key to ff. 80r, 88r, 92r; shared s/t and r/y signs and unidentified signs stop a full reading.

Second pass with cypher-7e's harley287 key (narrow/wide caret = s/t): sign copies from close crops of ff. 80r, 88r, 92r; the caret forms and the l/p/h loop signs could not be told apart, so only context guesses ('expences', 'of letters').

Third pass: sign inventory by eye at full resolution from about 60 glossed words on ff. 75, 79, 89 (signs.tsv); separates p/l/h/m/w; shows s/t, r/y, o/a and l/t share signs; glossed code numbers 7, 10, 15, 16.
Applied the inventory to ff. 80r, 88r, 92r: 'armada(s)', 'to these termes', 'the action', '15' = Parma, 'captain'; most runs still unread because of polyphonic and unglossed signs.

Candidate-set word solver (solve.py): each sign a set of letters from signs.tsv, readings scored against a 1588 CSP Foreign word list with Elizabethan spelling normalised and up to 1-2 edits; over 22 transcribed runs it confirms these/terms, armada, action, captain, letters, charge; long runs on ff. 88 and 92 find no words, pointing to transcription errors.

Solver loop 1: re-read f.80/f.88 runs at 2x full resolution against solver candidates; 'haven' (f.80 and f.88, fixes c=a and L=e) and 'so forwarde in the action that he promised Q[ueen]' (f.80) confirmed; f.88: 'have promised the haven of ...' to Parma.

Solver loops on deskewed lines of ff. 88, 92, 96v with leads from harley287 READING and CSP Foreign 1588 (Semple to Scotland): Italians, Antonio, deliverd, divers, number of, within France, servants, priests, Portugals(?), Bruges(?).

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The alphabet was rebuilt sign by sign from the contemporary interlinear decipherments of sibling Cobham letters in the same volume, Harley 287 (f. 75 R8488, f. 79 R8489, f. 89 R8493), then applied to ff. 80, 88, 92 with a word-candidate solver.
outcome.notes: Sign inventory and codes fixed from glossed siblings; about a third of cipher words read (H/M); remaining runs have polyphonic or unglossed signs.

gaps.item: f. 80r-81r (R8490) long run f.80g, codes 22, 27 and the square sign
gaps.detail: 22, 27 and the square are unglossed in the siblings R8481/R8488/R8489/R8493; run 80g gives no word even with two edits

gaps.item: f. 88r (R8492): name after 'captain', word after 'haven of', lines 3-6 and the seven cipher words of ll. 12-20 (recurring 'Tnn')
gaps.detail: signs K, upsilon, rho, W not glossed on any sibling; polyphonic signs (wedge s/t/a, gamma r/y, c o/a, phi l/t/p) leave several readings
solver finds no word with two edits; same unglossed and polyphonic signs

gaps.item: ff. 96r-97r (R8496), all but a few words (e.g. f. 96v line 4)
gaps.detail: only 'passed', 'within France', 'servants', 'priests' read; the rest turns on the same signs; f. 97r runs not in runs.txt

outcome.fraction_read_source: Not measurable: READING.md and reading_*.md list read words as fragments with grades, not aligned to the sign transcription in runs.txt (22 runs, ff. 80/88/92 only; f. 97r untranscribed), so no token count of read vs unread exists. 0.35 kept from the notes ('about a third of the cipher words read with grade H or M').

prior.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherments of sibling letters (DECODE R8488, R8493); these four letters not deciphered anywhere found; not in CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
